text: Armaz Akhvlediani - The authorities supported Metropolitan Shio, that is crystal clear, he was involved and still is - we saw this, and I have a suspicion that we will see it even before the start of the historic synod, where the Patriarch is supposed to be elected (28.04.2026, 19:37)

For the final session, where the Patriarch is to be chosen by the Synod, the configuration may change somewhat — Bishop Shio has been promoted, but I would not rush and would not draw a final conclusion, - politician Armaz Akhvlediani said in the “Resume” program on “Palitranews.”
According to Armaz Akhvlediani, everything will depend on where the votes of the other two candidates go.

“The main decision lies ahead; today the Synod session only selected the candidates. We already know the figures, who received how many votes. Let us not forget either that by the final session, where the Synod is to choose the Patriarch, it is not impossible that the configuration may change to some extent. However, today it is clear who has moved ahead: Bishop Shio has moved ahead, but I would not rush and would not draw a final conclusion, unlike others.”

“Today, the patriarch was not being elected; today only three candidates were nominated, and when one is to be chosen, the other two may agree on where their votes, as well as the votes of others, will go,” said Armaz Akhvlediani.
According to Armaz Akhvlediani, it is crystal clear that the government is interfering in the Patriarchate elections and supporting Bishop Shio.

“The authorities supported Bishop Shio, that is crystal clear. He was and is involved. Let’s say it directly: all government-aligned media, from morning till evening, actively, in every context, no matter what topic they were discussing, directly or indirectly supported this one candidate. If that is not interference, then what is interference?! As for interference by other means, I cannot speak about that; I have no facts. If I did, I would say so. But I have a well-founded suspicion and assumption that an ill-intentioned government always has levers of influence, pressure, and sway, especially a government whose authority has been destroyed and which needs to cling to something—in this case, the authority of the Church, gained by inertia—and use it for its own benefit. We have seen this over this period, and I suspect we will see it even before the start of the historical synod, where the final patriarch is supposed to be chosen,” said Armaz Akhvlediani.

For your information, the Holy Synod has selected three patriarchal candidates. According to the Synod’s decision, the candidates for the patriarchate will be: the locum tenens of the patriarchal throne, Metropolitan Shio (Mujiri) of Senaki and Chkhorotsku; Metropolitan Job of the Urbnisi and Ruisi eparchy; and Metropolitan Grigol of Poti and Khobi.

As the head of the Patriarchate’s Public Relations Service, Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze, told journalists, the locum tenens of the Patriarchal throne, Shio, received 20 votes, while the other two candidates received 7 votes each. He also explained that the other candidates were Metropolitan Grigol Katia, Metropolitan Dositeos, and Metropolitan Melkisedek.
